summary: Sudden TTFB increase for chat completions after customer pinned model and platform runtime rollout
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightAssist reports a sudden and sustained increase in time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completion requests after they pin a specific model version and after the platform runtime rollout on 2026-03-11. Impact is restricted to their prod us-east workloads and started ~2026-03-12 09:40 UTC.

Impact:
- Chat TTFB increased from ~120ms median to 700-1,200ms for initial tokens.
- End-user experience: noticeably slower streaming starts; some requests time out at client SDK layer after 10s (rare).
- No increased 5xx error rate observed, but elevated latencies causing SLA concerns for enterprise contract.

Environment:
- Customer is on enterprise Dedicated/Dual-mode (private control plane, hosted runtime).
- Customer had pinned model: redwood-open-1.4-quantized@2026-03-10.
- Platform runtime rolled out to us-east on 2026-03-11: runtime-agent 2.14 -> 2.16 (canary->region).

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer and validated by Support):
1) Send new chat completion request to pinned model endpoint using streaming=true.
2) Observe initial HTTP chunk and TTFB measured at client side (SDK).
3) Repeat with warm session (existing conversation) vs new session.

Observed behavior:
- New sessions show high TTFB (median ~800ms, p95 ~1.15s).
- Warm sessions (after previous calls) show normal TTFB (~140ms).
- Larger prompts (context >1k tokens) exacerbate delay slightly.
- Logs show normal token generation throughput once streaming starts.

Logs excerpt and metrics (selected):
- Serving runtime traces: request_enter -> model_load_hit=true -> kernel_dispatch_time increased for first token on quantized path.
- Per-route latency: initial-byte latency increased 6x while tail-of-stream latency unchanged.
- No obvious memory pressure or GPU OOM events in node metrics.

Additional notes:
- Customer uses dedicated pool with pinned model; we observed the same TTFB pattern when we duplicated request traffic in a test namespace that also upgraded to runtime 2.16.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) POST /v1/chat/completions to customer endpoint with streaming=true using pinned model. 2) Measure time from request send -> first chunk. 3) Compare cold session vs warm session. 4) Reproduce on an instance still on runtime 2.14 to confirm delta.
logs_excerpt:
[2026-03-12T09:42:11Z] request_id=abc123 serving-runtime: model_lookup hit=true; kv_cache_lookup miss; kernel_select start; kernel_select took 420ms; first_token_emit at 850ms; subsequent tokens at 25ms/token.
[2026-03-12T09:42:12Z] node-metrics: gpu_util=45% mem_ok=true; no OOM; batch_size=1;
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: kernel selection or quantized model path introduced a slow JIT/initialization path in runtime 2.16 that only affects first-token emission for cold contexts (e.g., KV cache miss or first forward pass after model pin).
Actions taken so far:
- Replayed customer traffic against a runtime-2.14 instance: no TTFB spike observed.
- Captured debug-level kernel dispatch traces and enabled extra timing for quantized operator init.
- Created INT ticket for runtime engineering to look at kernel dispatch fallbacks (INT-829).
- Temporarily routed BrightAssist traffic to a 2.14 pool as a mitigation for their SLA while engineering investigates.
hypothesis: A change in kernel selection logic in runtime 2.16 causes an extra CPU-bound initialization on the first execution of certain quantized kernels, adding ~400-600ms before the first token is emitted. Warm paths hit cached kernels and are unaffected.
root_cause: Under investigation by runtime team. Preliminary root cause: regression in kernel dispatch when model is quantized and pinned; fallback to a compatibility kernel path triggers per-request initialization on cold contexts. See related PR investigation.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: routed customer's requests to runtime 2.14 pool for us-east and created a temporary routing rule. Long-term fix: runtime patch to avoid per-request kernel init on quantized path (PR referenced below). Engineering ETA for patch and staged rollout: 2026-03-16.
Follow-ups: validate with synthetic cold-start tests across quantized models and add unit test to prevent regression.
